analysis.title: GS Ellinikaki - 10 for the weekend 2 Oct 2026
key_insights: US 10-yr yield reached 5.25% before softer macro data supported less Fed tightening and offered some duration relief.
GS Economics (David Mericle) pushed the next Fed hike from October to December after softer August core PCE and sees a strong chance that no further hikes are ultimately needed.

Rates desk (Will Marshall) says softer payrolls, downward revisions and weak wages reinforce that call and show no labour-driven inflation pressure. Against this week's credit stress, valuations, positioning and softer data are starting to set up renewed duration support.
Tony P views higher rates as a headwind to stocks, not a wrecking ball, absent an inflation surge or a credit problem, and expects healthy earnings growth.
Dom Wilson argues that after the repricing in yields, asymmetry has shifted to the constructive side ('More Paths to Relief').
Global Fundamental L/S hedge funds returned -0.55% in September, with positive alpha partly offsetting beta losses. YTD return is +12.6%.
Hedge fund positioning: Europe saw its largest percentage net buying in over five years, while HFs rotated into TMT in the US as almost every other sector was net sold.

Agentic AI debate has shifted from AI helping consumers discover products to agents acting for them. This raises disruption risk for search, telcos and insurers and raises the value of payments, identity and trust infrastructure.

Amazon was added to the GIR Conviction List. Eric Sheridan sees upside from above-Street AWS growth and margins, the orchestration layer, a ~$70bn Physical AI opportunity and digital advertising strength.

Internet team views agentic commerce as a 3-5+ year trend, analogous to the development of eCommerce, and names META, GOOGL, AMZN, V, MA, EFX, TRU, FICO, LYV, SHOP, NET, STUB, WMT, SN and TPR as long-term beneficiaries.

Telco team sees agentic AI re-basing telco FCF by reducing customer inertia, implying 5-20% medium-term FCF risk, partly mitigated by cost savings, lower distributor commissions and pricing power. Switzerland, UK, Norway and Belgium look most exposed. No estimate cuts for now given 3-5 year adoption, and the team remains bullish on the sector.

Conviction List changes. US adds: AMZN, BURL, HII, JCI, OXY. US removals: APD, COP, GLNG, LOAR, TSN. Europe adds: Solaria, Straumann, Scout24, IMCD. Europe removals: Naturgy, Norsk Hydro, Smith & Nephew. APAC adds: Kotak Mahindra Bank, NEC. APAC removals: Jardine Matheson, Foshan Haitian, Wuxi AppTec, Shenzhen Inovance.
Solaria addition is on data-centre optionality, with BBG reporting talks with Alibaba.

Evonik rejected a €10bn BASF approach. The initial proposal (€22.15) implies ~7x EBITDA, below prior sector deals, with synergies averaging 8% of target sales. An EC phase 2 review is plausible, so a deal would likely take 12m+ to close and trade at a substantial arb spread.
BASF and Evonik report Q3 on 28-Oct and 03-Nov. Investors are trading the 2031 convertible bonds as an alternative expression, and EVK can be hedged with GSCMEVON Index.
Sam Darbyshire initiates SalMar at Buy (22% upside) and Mowi at Neutral (8% upside). Tightening supply should lift salmon prices and EBIT per kg into 2027.

Sika remains a Conviction List stock. Q3 organic growth was +5.1% with better pricing and positive volumes, and FY26 growth is tracking to the top end of guidance. Pricing plus lower raw-material costs should drive 2027 margin and EPS upside.
Zegona: Mollie sees 70% upside, ~3% service revenue CAGR from Spanish telecom consolidation, FY29 FCF ~30% above consensus and a ~11% 2026 TSR yield.

tension_points.bull_case: Absent an inflation surge or credit problem, higher rates are a headwind, not a wrecking ball, and earnings growth stays healthy (Tony P). Softer payrolls and PCE push the next Fed hike to December and may end hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit stress this week and the 5.25% 10-yr peak show the risk that rates or credit break the earnings-driven bull case.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An inflation surge or a credit problem.

tension_points.bull_case: Telco team stays bullish and sees upside to consensus. Cost savings, lower distributor commissions and pricing power mitigate the impact, and adoption takes 3-5 years.
tension_points.bear_case: Agents negotiating phone and cable bills reduce customer inertia, implying 5-20% medium-term FCF risk, with Switzerland, UK, Norway and Belgium most exposed.
